correctness.rationale: In the simple symmetric K_{a,b} game (a,b≥1), an agent in U with old block type (u_i,v_i) strictly prefers a candidate (x,y) iff y*u_i>x*v_i; for W iff x*v_j>y*u_j. For each x,y≥1 independently choose x of A_pi(x,y) eligible U and y of B_pi(x,y) eligible W, giving the exact size polynomial and no duplicate coalitions; one-sided coalitions cannot strictly improve. Rational rank threshold sorting and binomial table yield the arithmetic-operation bound. In the a paired U-W plus m singleton W partition, paired W and paired U strict requirements conflict, so all selected W must be singletons: M(a,m)=sum_x sum_{y>x} C(a,x)C(m,y), m≤1 no blockers, m=2 exactly a blockers. For m=a+t√a+o(√a), 2^a ε=P(Y>X,X≥1)→Φ(t/√2) by binomial central limit; outside m/a→1 use Chebyshev. Formula does not use bit-complexity claims.
